arxiv-1506-00271.title: Degeneracies and fluctuations of Néèl skyrmions in confined geometries
arxiv-1506-00271.creator: Rick Keesman, A.O. Leonov, P. van Dieten, Stefan Buhrandt, G. T. Barkema, Lars Fritz, R.A. Duine
arxiv-1506-00271.description: Abstract The recent discovery of tunable Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in layered magnetic materials with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy makes them promising candidates for stabilization and manipulation of skyrmions at elevated temperatures. In this article, we use Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the robustness of skyrmions in these materials against thermal fluctuations and finite-size effects.

arxiv-2112-04008.title: Multinational Address Parsing: A Zero-Shot Evaluation
arxiv-2112-04008.creator: Marouane Yassine, David Beauchemin, François Laviolette, Luc Lamontagne
arxiv-2112-04008.description: Abstract Address parsing consists of identifying the segments that make up an address, such as a street name or a postal code. Because of its importance for tasks like record linkage, address parsing has been approached with many techniques, the latest relying on neural networks.

arxiv-2301-05489.title: A Residual Diffusion Model for High Perceptual Quality Codec Augmentation
arxiv-2301-05489.creator: Noor Fathima Ghouse*, Jens Petersen*, Auke Wiggers*, Tianlin Xu, Guillaume Sautière {noor, jpeterse, auke, gsautie}@qti.qualcomm.com; tianlin.xu1@gmail.com
arxiv-2301-05489.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Noor Fathima Ghouse*, Jens Petersen*, Auke Wiggers*, Tianlin Xu, Guillaume Sautière {noor, jpeterse, auke, gsautie}@qti.qualcomm.com; tianlin.xu1@gmail.com. Diffusion probabilistic models have recently achieved remarkable success in generating high quality image and video data. In this work, we build on this class of generative models and introduce a method for lossy compression of high resolution images.

arxiv-2407-18859.title: A Tauberian characterization of the Riemann hypothesis through the floor function
arxiv-2407-18859.creator: Benoit Cloitre
arxiv-2407-18859.description: Abstract We introduce a new Tauberian framework through the theory of "regular arithmetic functions". This allows us to establish a characterization of the Riemann hypothesis by linking the floor function to the distribution of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

arxiv-2503-23179.title: OncoReg: Medical Image Registration for Oncological Challenges
arxiv-2503-23179.creator: \firstname Wiebke \surname Heyer \aff 1, \firstname Yannic \surname Elser \aff 2, \firstname Lennart \surname Berkel \aff 2, \firstname Xinrui \surname Song \aff 3, \firstname Xuanang \surname Xu \aff 3, \firstname Pingkun \surname Yan \aff 3, \firstname Xi \surname Jia \aff 4, \firstname Jinming \s
arxiv-2503-23179.description: Abstract In modern cancer research, the vast volume of medical data generated is often underutilised due to challenges related to patient privacy. The OncoReg Challenge addresses this issue by enabling researchers to develop and validate image registration methods through a two-phase framework that ensures patient privacy while fostering the development of more generalisable AI models.

arxiv-2507-08091.title: Low-rank Momentum Factorization for Memory Efficient Training
arxiv-2507-08091.creator: Pouria Mahdavinia pxm5426@psu.edu, Mehrdad Mahdavi mzm616@psu.edu
arxiv-2507-08091.description: Abstract Fine-tuning large foundation models presents significant memory challenges due to stateful optimizers like AdamW, often requiring several times more GPU memory than inference. While memory-efficient methods like parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA) and optimizer state compression exist, recent approaches like GaLore bridge these by using low-rank gradient projections and subspace moment accumulation.

arxiv-2512-00624.title: Rotational Light-Curve Recovery & Predictions of the LSST Yield of Hildas
arxiv-2512-00624.creator: Alexander J. Fleming, Jacob A. Kurlander, Dmitrii E. Vavilov, David Vokrouhlický, David Nesvorný, Pedro H. Bernardinelli, Mario Jurić
arxiv-2512-00624.description: Abstract The Hilda population occupies the stable 3:2 mean-motion resonance of Jupiter and provides a window into Solar System evolution, including collisional processes. The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will conduct the ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

arxiv-2512-06198.title: Cascaded Tightly-Coupled Observer Design for Single-Range-Aided Inertial Navigation This work was supported by the National Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC), under the grants NSERC-DG RGPIN 2020-06270 and NSERC-DG RGPIN-2020-04759
arxiv-2512-06198.creator: Oussama Sifour, Soulaimane Berkane, Abdelhamid Tayebi
arxiv-2512-06198.description: Abstract This work introduces a single-range-aided navigation observer that reconstructs the full state of a rigid body using only an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), a body-frame vector measurement ( e.g., magnetometer), and a distance measurement from a fixed anchor point. The design first formulates an extended linear time-varying (LTV) system to estimate body-frame position, body-frame velocity, and the gravity direction.

arxiv-2602-11103.title: GameDevBench: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Through Game Development
arxiv-2602-11103.creator: Wayne Chi, Yixiong Fang, Arnav Yayavaram, Siddharth Yayavaram, Seth Karten, Qiuhong Anna Wei, Runkun Chen, Alexander Wang, Valerie Chen, Ameet Talwalkar, Chris Donahue

pmc-10624765.creator: Ghofran Jaha, Bader AlMutairi
pmc-10624765.description: The Mullerian ducts give rise to the upper part of the female reproductive system, including the uterus, cervix, upper two-thirds of the vagina, and fallopian tubes, which undergo specific processes of development, fusion, and resorption. Any failure in this process will lead to Mullerian duct anomaly (MDA).

pmc-11332878.title: Protocol for differentiation of monocytes and macrophages from human induced pluripotent stem cells
pmc-11332878.creator: Kevin Emmerich, Francesca Calcaterra, Xuming Tang, Guibin Chen, Elena Pontarini, Roberta Ciceri, Dan Yang, Benjamin Joseph, Silvia Della Bella, Isabella Varea, Domenico Mavilio, Manfred Boehm

Here, we present a protocol for differentiation of monocytes and macrophages from hiPSCs.

pmc-12408402.title: Real-time converter of intermittent-scanned glucose sensors to continuous glucose monitors with potential future applications for insulin delivery
pmc-12408402.creator: Pablo S Rivadeneira, Alejandro Mira
pmc-12408402.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper presents the development of a transmitter that transforms intermittent glucose sensors (isCGM) into a continuous and real-time glucose monitoring system (c-rtCGM), a key component in automated insulin delivery systems. The transmitter enhances the capabilities of conventional intermittent sensors by leveraging Near Field Communication (NFC) technology to capture raw glucose value and automatically transmit it via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE-Bluetooth 4.2 Dual-Mode) to a smart device every five minutes.

pmc-12412607.title: The Pathophysiological Role of Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress in Rheumatic Diseases
pmc-12412607.creator: Zhao Ma, Qiaoping Xu, Xinchang Xu
pmc-12412607.description: Mitochondria play a crucial role in reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent rheumatic diseases, including ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis (OA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and scleroderma. Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), which encodes mitochondrial proteins, is more vulnerable to oxidants compared to nuclear DNA. When mtDNA gets damaged, it leads to mitochondrial dysfunction, such as electron transport chain impairment and loss of mitochondrial membrane potential.

pmc-12567442.title: Differential Induction of Resistance Mechanisms by Methyl Jasmonate in Two Vaccinium corymbosum L. Cultivars Under Combined Water Deficit and Aluminum Toxicity

pmc-13035050.title: A binary prototype for time-series surveillance and intervention
pmc-13035050.creator: Jason Olejarz, Till Hoffmann, Alex Zapf, Douaa Mugahid, Ross Molinaro, Chadwick Brown, Artem Boltyenkov, Taras Dudykevych, Ankit Gupta, Marc Lipsitch, Rifat Atun, Jukka-Pekka Onnela, Sarah Fortune, Rangarajan Sampath, Yonatan H. Grad
pmc-13035050.description: Despite much research on early detection of anomalies from surveillance data, a systematic framework for appropriately acting on these signals is lacking. We addressed this gap by formulating a hidden Markov-style model for time-series surveillance, where the system state, the observed data, and the decision rule are all binary.

pmc-13176100.title: Optimization and verification of high‐fat diet formulation for establishing a rat model of obesity‐related precocious puberty
pmc-13176100.creator: Jiayi Gong, Wei Qian, Deji Song, Kang Li, Li Zhang, Li Shi
pmc-13176100.description: Childhood obesity is closely linked to the rising incidence of precocious puberty (PP), yet valid preclinical models of obesity‐related PP remain lacking. High‐fat diets (HFD) are widely used for obesity models, but the suitability of different HFD formulations for inducing PP is unknown.

pmc-13422836.title: Ultrasound-guided sacral multifidus plane block versus caudal epidural block for postoperative analgesia in pediatric hypospadias surgery: A randomized double-blind controlled trial
pmc-13422836.creator: Amr Sobhy, Radwa Tarek Mohamed, Gihan seif, Manal mohamed kamal shams, Adham Magdy Haggag, Abd El-Aziz A. Abd EL-Aziz
pmc-13422836.description: IntroductionHypospadias repair is associated with moderate to severe postoperative pain in children. Caudal epidural block is traditionally considered the standard regional anesthetic technique for sub-umbilical pediatric surgeries; however, its duration of analgesia and potential adverse effects may be limited. The sacral multifidus plane block (SMPB) is a novel ultrasound-guided fascial plane technique that may provide prolonged analgesia with fewer complications.

pmc-13429482.title: Honeybee aging as an emergent property of a self-organizing dissipative system
pmc-13429482.creator: Radmila Čapková Frydrychová
pmc-13429482.description: The honeybee colony provides a remarkable example of aging plasticity emerging from collective biological organization. Through the reciprocal regulation of juvenile hormone (JH) and vitellogenin (Vg), honeybees demonstrate that aging is a dynamic and reversible process shaped by social and environmental conditions.
